blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Earning trust with British clients is a patient, layered process. It begins with small promises kept — replying to an email when you said you would, delivering a draft when you said you would, showing up on time to a call you requested. The British notice these tiny signals long before they notice a big pitch.

It continues with admitting when you are wrong. A British client who watches you admit a small error quickly, without defensiveness, will trust you with a bigger one later. The worst thing is to pretend nothing happened.

And it deepens with consistency over time. Three good months build nothing. Three good years open doors. The British pace is slow, but the reward is disproportionate — a trusted adviser relationship that competitors find almost impossible to break.

items.q: According to the text, what do British clients notice first?
options: Tiny signals, like small promises kept
items.why: "The British notice these tiny signals long before they notice a big pitch."

items.q: What effect does admitting a small error quickly have?
options: It leads the client to trust you with a bigger matter later
It makes no difference either way
It forces the client to renegotiate the contract
items.why: "will trust you with a bigger one later" — admitir um erro pequeno abre espaço para mais confiança.

items.q: What does "Three good months build nothing. Three good years open doors" suggest?
options: Trust with British clients is earned only over the long term
British clients change suppliers every year
Monthly results are all that matter
items.why: Inferência: o contraste meses × anos mostra que a confiança britânica se constrói no longo prazo.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: A brilliant pitch wins a British client's trust straight away.
A quick, non-defensive apology can strengthen a relationship.
Consistency over years matters more than a single impressive meeting.
items.why: Inferência: o texto todo defende que a confiança é lenta e feita de pequenos sinais — não de um pitch brilhante imediato.

items.q: The phrase "the reward is disproportionate" suggests that…
options: the payoff is far larger than the slow pace would imply
British clients pay above market rates
items.why: Inferência: "disproportionate" aqui é positivo — o retorno supera de longe o ritmo lento do processo.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James apresentar a carteira de clientes do Reino Unido ao novo diretor de vendas. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, before I hand you this client book, let me tell you how it was actually built. Take Harrington's — the account everyone assumes was easy. It took us three years to become their trusted adviser. Three years.

The first year, honestly, we won nothing big. We just kept turning up. If I said I would send a draft by Thursday, it landed on Thursday. If I promised to call at nine, I called at nine. None of it felt impressive at the time.

The turning point came when we got a forecast wrong. My predecessor rang them the same morning, said plainly that we had missed it, and set out how we would fix it. No excuses, no pretending it hadn't happened. They told me later that was the moment they decided to trust us with the bigger mandate.

So when you meet these clients, don't lead with a clever pitch. Reply when you say you will. Deliver when you say you will. And if you slip, own it fast. That is the whole game here — and it is why these relationships are so hard for competitors to prise away.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How long did it take to become Harrington's trusted adviser?
items.why: "It took us three years to become their trusted adviser."

items.q: What did they mainly do in the first year?
options: Kept small promises and turned up reliably
Delivered a series of impressive pitches
items.why: "We just kept turning up… drafts on Thursday, calls at nine" — pequenos compromissos cumpridos.

items.q: What happened at the turning point?
options: The team hid the mistake to protect the relationship
James won a new pitch competition
The predecessor admitted a wrong forecast the same morning
items.why: "My predecessor rang them the same morning, said plainly that we had missed it."

items.q: Why does James say the client decided to trust them with the bigger mandate?
options: Because the forecast was actually correct
Because the honest, fast admission of the error impressed them
items.why: Inferência: foi a franqueza rápida diante do erro — não o erro em si — que gerou a confiança maior.

items.q: What is James's main advice to the new director?
options: Reply and deliver on time, and own any slip quickly
Lead with a clever pitch to stand out
Focus on winning big accounts fast
Avoid admitting mistakes to protect credibility
items.why: "Don't lead with a clever pitch. Reply when you say you will. Deliver when you say you will. And if you slip, own it fast."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Earning trust with British clients is a patient, layered process." Here patient means…
items.why: Patient = paciente: exige persistência calma ao longo do tempo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "If you promise a draft by Friday, ___ it by Friday — the timing is a trust signal."
items.why: To deliver = entregar; cumprir o prazo prometido é o sinal de confiança.

items.q: "She met the mistake with no defensiveness at all." Defensiveness is…
options: an instinct to protect yourself instead of owning the error
items.why: Defensiveness = postura defensiva: proteger-se em vez de assumir o erro.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The relationship deepens with ___ — the same reliable behaviour repeated over years."
items.why: Consistency = consistência: o mesmo comportamento confiável, repetido no tempo.

items.q: "The slow pace brings a disproportionate reward." Disproportionate here means the reward is…
options: far larger than the pace would suggest
items.why: Disproportionate = desproporcional: o retorno é muito maior do que o ritmo lento faria esperar.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em conversas sobre clientes e confiança. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "When we missed the forecast, she owned up to it the same morning." To own up to something means to…
items.why: Own up to = assumir a responsabilidade, admitir o erro.

items.q: "We will build up trust one small promise at a time." To build up means to…
items.why: Build up = construir/aumentar aos poucos, gradualmente.

items.q: "A trusted-adviser relationship is hard for competitors to break into." To break into means to…
options: manage to enter or win a share of
items.why: Break into = conseguir entrar/penetrar (um mercado ou relação já estabelecida).

items.q: "The team agreed to reply on time, but they never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim aquilo que foi combinado.

items.q: "Turning up on time won't move the needle in one week, but it does over years." To move the needle means to…
items.why: Move the needle = fazer diferença perceptível, mexer o ponteiro.
